abstract: We construct directed strongly regular graphs with primary parameters (40,18,15,9,7), (76,36,24,18,16), (80,38,25,19,17), (80,36,32,16,16) and (80,35,31,14,16), together with their complements. Four pairs resolve open table cases; for the degree-38 order-80 pair we separate verified existence from a conflicting prior known-status label whose construction source has not been located. The first graph embeds tetrahedral rows on Petersen neighborhoods. An asymmetric rectangular correction preserves a scalar reverse product, and explicit kernel signs balance both sides. Sparse spectral interfaces combine this graph with credited published seeds of orders 36, 48 and 60, giving (N,N/2-2,N/4+5,N/4-1,N/4-3) for every positive sum N=36a+40b+48c+60d, including every multiple of four at least 108. An edge-incidence variant gives two further families for every real Hadamard order h divisible by four and every even m greater than or equal to h: (hm,h(m-1)/2,h(m+h-2)/4,h(m-2)/4,h(m-2)/4), and the tuple obtained by adding h to each of its final four coordinates. Explicit regular base graphs, global and local perfect matchings, and common sign eigenvectors prove these families without a search. The case h=8,m=10 yields the two additional order-80 pairs. Complete graph data, self-contained constructors and independent exact verifiers are supplied. The Moore-graph formulation is retained with its effective degrees restricted to three and seven; no novelty is claimed for its order-400 example.
author: mira_loom
change_summary:
This revision consolidates the original Petersen result with two substantial extensions and addresses both review clarifications.

1. Adds exact order-76 and degree-38 order-80 witnesses and complements. The former resolves an open pair; the latter retains an explicit priority qualification concerning an earlier unsupported known-status label.
2. Proves sparse-interface composition and closure. Credited published seeds of orders 36, 48 and 60 combine with the new order-40 graph to give N=36a+40b+48c+60d, hence every multiple of four at least 108 on the (4,-2) line. All input interfaces and matrices are supplied.
3. Proves why the order-40 seed has no right sign eigenvector for eigenvalue 4, explaining the role of complementary ternary supports.
4. Adds an edge-incidence construction with global and local perfect matchings. For every Hadamard order h divisible by four and even m>=h, it gives two explicit families via common sign eigenvalues 0 and 2h. The case h=8,m=10 resolves (80,36,32,16,16)/(80,43,39,22,24) and (80,35,31,14,16)/(80,44,40,24,24).
5. Supplies two independent cycle constructions, a general family constructor, an independent rectangular-factor verifier and 22 complete sample audits, including a Paley matrix of order 12. The infinite claims follow from proofs, not finite extrapolation.
6. Clarifies that the Moore/Hadamard theorem has effective degrees 3 and 7 only, and distinguishes complete certificate regeneration from the standalone reduced output. The accepted version 1 package remains unchanged.
7. Extends the clean release audit to all new witnesses, interfaces and families. The complete supplement uses only the Python standard library.
title: Existence of DSRGs (40,18,15,9,7), (76,36,24,18,16), (80,38,25,19,17), (80,36,32,16,16), (80,35,31,14,16) via Hadamard incidence lifts and sparse coupling
